## [17] Unravelling the Role of Intraspecific Variability in the Coexistence of Tropical Forest Tree Species
<hr />

{{< fa calendar-days >}}&nbsp; June 2026
<br/>{{< fa user >}}&nbsp; **Ghislain Vieilledent** (CIRAD, France) 
<br/>{{< fa user >}}&nbsp; **Isabelle Maréchaux** (INRAE, France) 
<br/>{{< fa globe >}}&nbsp; [INTRACO](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/the-frb-in-action/programs-and-projects/le-cesab/intraco/) project

<br/>

**Abstract**

Hundreds of tree species can coexist within a single hectare of tropical forest. 
Several mechanisms have been proposed to explain how so many species can stably 
coexist while competing for a limited number of resources (mainly light, water, and nutrients). 
Among these mechanisms, the role of intraspecific variability (IV), which is large 
in tree communities, has only been recently considered. Studies that have so far 
explored the effect of IV on species coexistence focused on species-poor systems, 
used disparate approaches, and reached contrasting results. IV can result from genetic 
variability and could make species less different, hindering their stable coexistence. 
A different view is that observed IV is primarily the result of fine-scale environmental 
variability and could reveal differences among species on unobserved dimensions, promoting 
species coexistence. [INTRACO](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/the-frb-in-action/programs-and-projects/le-cesab/intraco/) proposes to provide a clear synthesis of the effect of 
IV on species coexistence in hyperdiverse communities combining literature review, 
empirical data-set analyses, and both theoretical and data-based models. 
Our results will help understand and predict changes in biodiversity in a global change context.
